title: Creating a Secret Manager Decoy in GCP

blocks.text: A secret manager in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is a service used to securely store, manage, and control access to sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, certificates, and tokens. Secrets are stored centrally and accessed by applications through authenticated requests based on IAM permissions. You can create secret manager decoys containing fake secret identifiers or access references. Any attempt to access or enumerate these decoy secrets is detected and logged as an attack. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Zscaler Deception dashboard.
Before creating a secret manager decoy in GCP, ensure that you have configured the integration between GCP and Deception.
To create a secret manager decoy:

blocks.item: Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Secret Manager.
Click Add Decoy.
See image.
The GCP Secret Manager drawer appears.
In the GCP Secret Manager drawer:
Project: Select the project in which you want to create the decoy.
Name: Enter a name for the secret manager decoy.
Description: Enter a description for the secret manager decoy.
See image.
Click Save.
If you want to add multiple secret manager decoys to GCP, repeat the previous steps for each decoy and then deploy all decoys simultaneously.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings.
Locate the GCP project you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the gcp-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the gcp-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform:
export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"
Run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to export the state file as JSON:
terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json
The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings, locate the GCP project you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

Upon successful deployment, the secret manager decoy is added to GCP. The deployment status is indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the secret manager decoys table (Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Secret Manager) within the Deception Admin Portal. To learn how to configure lures using secret manager decoys, see Configuring Lures Using GCP Decoys.
